titleStmt.title: To Harriet Shaw Weaver. Saturday, 11 August 1917
titleStmt.author: James Joyce

seriesStmt.p: Machine readable texts of the unpublished correspondence of James Joyce

projectDesc.p: James Joyce's unpublished correspondence, collected, annotated, and made available as a digital edition

div.p:
Dear Miss Weaver: I send signed copy of my novel for Mr Frank Albert, 3 Townshend Road, Richmond, Surrey. It may advertise the book. Please place the amount to my account and I shall remit the balance due by me on last dozen copies. The name of the bookseller is Ebell. If you are short of copies perhaps the printers could do you a hundred for next month before I correct the proofs. I suppose there are not many mistakes. My corrections could then be used for the rest of the edition. It would be a pity to lose orders. The critic I told you of has already a copy given him by me. The Semaine
Litteraire Littéraire
, I suppose, is in Lausanne. A card to G.P.O. Geneva would set matters right if the book has not been returned. Have you any news of the Italian papers?

div.note: JJ sent a signed copy of A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man for the bookseller Frank Albert in reply to Harriet Weaver’s question in her letter of 31 July 1917: “If I were to send out a copy of your novel would you be willing to sign it for the bookseller a letter from whom I enclose?” (Firth 175-76).

C. M. Ebell, book and art dealer, 1 Bahnhofstrasse 14, Zurich. In reply to Harriet Weaver’s comment in her letter of 31 July 1917: “You speak of trying to get some wholesale bookseller in Zurich to take copies on sale” (Firth 175).

There had been some confusion as to the paper’s name and address. Harriet Weaver wrote to JJ on 31 July 1917: “I have now had a letter from Mr. Jaffé who advises that a copy be sent to the Semaine Litteraire, Lausanne, as well as to the Journal de Génève and he says that he mentioned this paper to you. Are there [these?], I wonder, the two papers of the same name or is it a case of absentmindedness on your part or on his)? You had told me the Semaine Litteraire, Geneva and I sent the copy there. I shall not send one to Lausanne until I hear from you again on the matter” (Firth 175).
JJ and Harriet Weaver had been trying to interest Italian reviewers in A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (Firth 176).
